To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

amantadines block influenza virus release by causing a conformational change to the viral HA which occurs late in its transport through the secretory pathway and is triggered by a reduction in the pH of the intravesicular compartments.

amantadines inhibit influenza virus replication by blocking the M2 ion channel and that this action causes an acidification of the endocytic pathway that leads to a conformational change of the haemagluttinin that is necessary for virus infectivity.

Amantadine blocks the release of H7 virus particles from infected cells by inhibiting an M2 protein function that is important for protecting the acid‐sensitivie HA from the low pH environment in the exocytic compartment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the mechanism of action of amantadine and its analogs.
the mechanism of action of amantadine on the influenza virus.
elucidating the mechanisms of drug action and the nature of the molecular target.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amantadine‐sensitive M2 protein of influenza virus plays a role in the regulation of intracellular pH and is involved in the acid activation of the viral haemagglutin.
amantadines block the release of influenza viruses by interfering with the acidification of the intracellular compartments of the secretory pathway.
amantadines block the release of virus by inhibiting the M2 protein which is required for acidification of the vesicular compartments in the exocytic pathways of the infected cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

amantadines inhibit influenza virus by blocking a proton pump in the M2 protein of the influenza virus, and that the pump is involved in maintaining an acidic pH in endosomes and other compartments of the exo/endocytic pathway.
the M2 protein is involved in the transport and/or insertion of HA into the membrane and that the drug acts to prevent this process by interfering with the function of M1 and/or M2.
amantadines are a class of compounds which inhibit the function of the M2 protein of the influenza virus, which is responsible for the maintenance of a pH of approximately 7.5 in endocytic vesicles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
M2 is involved in counterbalancing the acidity of the endosome.
the M2 protein is important for the transport of the viral glycoproteins to the cell surface.
the M2 protein of influenza A is involved in maintaining the pH of the endocytic compartments of infected cells.
